extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, and authors of biomedical/clinical research manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: A 34-item structured index for evaluating the quality of a biomedical research report/manuscript across sections (title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Designed for reviewers/editors to score specific report features rather than give a single global judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title is clear, accurate, and informative.
rubrics_metrics.description: Title is clear, accurate, and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract reflects the content of the article.
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract reflects the content of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract is structured and includes objective, design, setting, patients, intervention, measurements, results, conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract is structured and includes objective, design, setting, patients, intervention, measurements, results, conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background information is sufficient and well-referenced.
rubrics_metrics.description: Background information is sufficient and well-referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis or objective is clearly stated.
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothesis or objective is clearly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance / relevance of the study is established.
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance / relevance of the study is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design is clearly described and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.description: Study design is clearly described and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study population / sample selection is fully described.
rubrics_metrics.description: Study population / sample selection is fully described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are stated.
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size is justified (power calculation if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size is justified (power calculation if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, a power calculation or other justification for sample size should be presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and timeframe of the study are stated.
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting and timeframe of the study are stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention or exposure is described in sufficient detail to replicate.
rubrics_metrics.description: Intervention or exposure is described in sufficient detail to replicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures are clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome measures are clearly defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods are clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical methods are clearly described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence intervals or precision measures are specified.
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence intervals or precision measures are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report precision (e.g., confidence intervals) for estimates rather than or in addition to p-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of dealing with missing data and dropouts are stated.
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of dealing with missing data and dropouts are stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe handling of missing data, imputation, and reasons for dropouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographics and baseline characteristics of the sample are reported.
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographics and baseline characteristics of the sample are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers of subjects analysed in each stage are reported (flow of participants).
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers of subjects analysed in each stage are reported (flow of participants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include participant flow (e.g., CONSORT-like reporting) showing numbers screened, enrolled, lost, analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcomes are reported with appropriate precision.
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcomes are reported with appropriate precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence intervals are given for primary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence intervals are given for primary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide CI/precision for primary outcome estimates to convey uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup analyses are clearly identified (a priori vs post hoc).
rubrics_metrics.description: Subgroup analyses are clearly identified (a priori vs post hoc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish pre-specified subgroup analyses from exploratory/post-hoc analyses and interpret accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative findings are reported.
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative findings are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report null or negative results rather than selectively reporting positive findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures are clear, accurate, and necessary.
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and figures are clear, accurate, and necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant or extraneous tables/figures; ensure clarity and accurate labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse events / unexpected findings are reported.
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse events / unexpected findings are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report harms and unexpected findings transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings are summarised accurately.
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings are summarised accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary should accurately reflect results without overstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of the study are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations of the study are discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit discussion of study limitations is expected; this item showed large reviewer-driven improvement in the original study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability of findings is appropriately considered.
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalisability of findings is appropriately considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider external validity and applicability to other populations/settings; flagged as a high-yield reviewer intervention in the original study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings are placed in context of prior literature.
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings are placed in context of prior literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how results align or contrast with existing studies and explain discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone of conclusions is appropriate to the strength of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone of conclusions is appropriate to the strength of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating implications; moderation of conclusion tone was among the largest improvements after review in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions follow from the data.
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions follow from the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure conclusions are logically supported by results and analyses presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for practice are discussed where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.description: Implications for practice are discussed where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, discuss practical/clinical implications while acknowledging limits of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations are accurate and reflect the cited works.
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations are accurate and reflect the cited works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure references correctly support statements and are accurately cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements include funding, conflicts of interest, and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements include funding, conflicts of interest, and contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources, potential conflicts of interest, and author/contributor roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall manuscript quality is high.
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall manuscript quality is high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A global item capturing the overall perceived report quality in addition to the section-specific items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item scoring scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item is scored on a 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score each of the 34 items individually rather than offering a single global judgement; use the numeric scores to identify strengths/weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer impact / high-yield interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical finding: the largest improvements after peer review/editing were on discussion of limitations (item 26), generalisability (item 27), use of confidence intervals (item 20), and tone of conclusions (item 29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items represent high-yield targets for reviewer comments and editorial intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational norms for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance: use the 34-item index as a structured pre-flight checklist before writing the review and devote particular attention to high-yield items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the index systematically, score all items, and emphasize improvements in limitations, generalisability, reporting of confidence intervals, and appropriate conclusion tone.
